nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلأَنْفَالِ قُلِ ٱلأَنفَالُ للَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: It was revealed on the day of Badr.
And Isrāʾīl narrated, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from his father, who said: "I came by a sword on the day of Badr and admired it, so I said: O Messenger of Allah, give it to me! So there was revealed ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلأَنْفَالِ قُلِ ٱلأَنفَالُ للَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ﴾."
Abū Jaʿfar said: What is known of the reading of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ is ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ ٱلأَنْفَالَ﴾ without (عَنْ); thus Shuʿba narrated it, from Simāk, from Muṣʿab, from his father.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ said on the day of Badr: "Whoever kills someone shall have such-and-such, and whoever takes a captive shall have such-and-such." When victory was granted to them, they came seeking that. Then Saʿd and the elders stood up and said: O Messenger of Allah, we took up this position only as a support for you, not out of cowardice. So there was revealed ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلأَنْفَالِ﴾, and they handed over the booty to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then afterwards there was revealed ﴿واعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُمْ مِنْ شَيءٍ فَأَنَّ للهِ خُمُسَهُ﴾.
So Allah, Mighty and Glorious, made clear in this that the anfāl came to be from the fifth (al-khumus), not from the whole.
Mujāhid and ʿIkrima said: It is abrogated; it was abrogated by ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ مَاغَنِمْتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ للهِ خُمُسَهُ﴾ to the end of the verse.
Mujāhid said: And al-anfāl are: the spoils.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And al-anfāl in the language are what the imām gives voluntarily, of what is not obligatory upon him, such as his saying: "Whoever brings a captive shall have such-and-such"; and from it comes al-nāfila (supererogatory) among the prayers. Then booty was called nafal because it is narrated "that spoils were not made lawful for anyone except the community of Muḥammad ﷺ", so it is as though they were given them as an extra gift (nāfila).
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَأَصْلِحُواْ ذَاتَ بِيْنِكُمْ﴾
Al-dhāt is: the reality; and al-bayn is: the bond; and from it comes ﴿لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَيُنَزِّلُ عَلَيْكُم مِّن ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً لِّيُطَهِّرَكُمْ بِهِ﴾. [Verse 11]
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The idolaters got to the water at Badr before the Muslims, so the Muslims remained thirsty, in a state of minor and major ritual impurity, unable to reach the water. Then Satan whispered to them, saying: You claim that you are upon the truth and that the Prophet is among you, yet your enemy has the water and you cannot reach it. So Allah, Mighty and Glorious, sent down the rain, and they drank from it until they were quenched, washed themselves, and watered their mounts.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: They quenched their thirst with the water, and the dust settled.
And someone else said: That was one of the great signs, because they were on salty marshy ground on which feet would not stay firm; when the rain came their feet became firm.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَيُذْهِبَ عَنكُمْ رِجْزَ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: That is, his whisperings.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: As for His saying ﴿وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ ٱلأَقْدَامَ﴾, there was in it [i.e. the place] a little stretch of sand on which no one could stand; when the rain came, the feet became firm upon it.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِذْ يُوحِي رَبُّكَ إِلَى ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ أَنِّي مَعَكُمْ فَثَبِّتُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: make them firm with something that you cast into their hearts.
And it is possible that the meaning is: make them firm by giving victory and fighting on their behalf.
* And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿فَٱضْرِبُواْ فَوْقَ ٱلأَعْنَاقِ﴾.
It has been said that "فوق" here is redundant (zāʾida), and that they were simply permitted to strike them in every way.
And what indicates this is ﴿وَٱضْرِبُواْ مِنْهُمْ كُلَّ بَنَانٍ﴾, because al-banān are the fingertips, the singular being banāna, derived from their saying أَبَنَّ بالمكان when he stayed in the place.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿ذٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ شَآقُّواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ﴾.
That is, they opposed, as though they had gone over to another side (shiqq).

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿يَآأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِذَا لَقِيتُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ زَحْفاً فَلاَ تُوَلُّوهُمُ ٱلأَدْبَارَ﴾.
That is, when you meet them face to face; one says: زحفتُ له, when you stood firm.
And it has been said: al-tazāḥuf is drawing near and approaching, that is, advancing slowly towards one another.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَمَن يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ دُبُرَهُ إِلاَّ مُتَحَرِّفاً لِّقِتَالٍ أَوْ مُتَحَيِّزاً إِلَىٰ فِئَةٍ فَقَدْ بَآءَ بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: This was for the day of Badr specifically, and fleeing from the advancing army is not one of the major sins.
And Shuʿba narrated from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from Abū Naḍra, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: It was revealed on the day of Badr. Abū Jaʿfar related to us, saying: Ibn Samāʿa related to us, saying: Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad related to us, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from Abū Naḍra, from Abū Saʿīd: ﴿وَمَن يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ دُبُرَهُ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ﴾ — he said: That was the day of Badr.
And ʿAṭāʾ said: It is abrogated by His saying ﴿فَإِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ مِائَةٌ صَابِرَةٌ يَغْلِبُوا مِائَتَيْنِ﴾. The people of Badr had no leader to withdraw to [other than him], since the Prophet ﷺ was with them, so it was not for them to prefer their own lives over his.
And in the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar: "We swerved aside [in flight] in an army and were afraid, so we said: O Messenger of Allah, we are the deserters. He said: I am your company (fiʾa)."
And likewise ʿUmar said on the day of al-Qādisiyya: I am the company of every Muslim.
And it has been said: This is general, because that is the ruling of "مَنْ" (whoever), unless some proof occurs. So if a man fears for his life and is certain that he has no power against the idolaters, he may withdraw, so as not to cast himself into destruction.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ﴾.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: [This was] when this one said: I killed, and that one said: I killed!
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَمَىٰ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: This was when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pelted them with pebbles.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The real sense of this in the language is that they were addressed according to what they knew, because their number was small and they were made to reach [their aim] against the idolaters [Translator's note: the phrase «وأُبلغُوا من المشركين» is unclear in the source; rendered literally]. And it is narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pelted them with [a handful of pebbles from] his palm, and there remained none of the idolaters but that some of it fell into his eye; that is, had it depended on what was in the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it would not have reached that great army, but Allah did that to them.
And the implied sense — and Allah knows best — is: You did not throw terror into their hearts when you threw the pebbles into their faces and said: "May the faces be disfigured!", but Allah threw terror into their hearts.
And it has been said: The meaning is: You did not throw the throw by which the killing occurred, but Allah threw.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَلِيُبْلِيَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْهُ بَلاۤءً حَسَناً﴾.
And al-balāʾ here is: favour.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِن تَسْتَفْتِحُواْ فَقَدْ جَآءَكُمُ ٱلْفَتْحُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, if you seek victory.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Abū Jahl said: "O Allah, give victory to whichever of the two parties is dearer to You." So Allah, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿إِن تَسْتَفْتِحُواْ فَقَدْ جَآءَكُمُ ٱلْفَتْحُ﴾.
And the meaning according to the philologists is: if you call for al-fatḥ, which is victory.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
And His saying [Translator's note: the source has the typo «وقوبه» for «وقوله»], Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: That is, they were afraid; and the philologists recited:
لَعَمْرُكَ مَا أَدْرِي وَإنِّي لأوجَلُ * عَلَى أَيِّنَا تَغْدُوا المَنِيَّةُ أَوَّلُ
(By your life, I do not know — and I am indeed afraid — upon which of us death will come first.)
And Sufyān narrated from al-Suddī concerning His saying, Mighty and Glorious, ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾: He said: When he intends to commit an injustice and it is said to him: Fear Allah, he refrains and his heart is afraid.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَإِذَا تُلِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُهُ زَادَتْهُمْ إِيمَاناً﴾
That is, they believed in them and so increased in faith.
Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ﴾ the five, with their ablution, their bowing, their prostration and their humility.
And Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said: Establishing it is that you keep to its times, perform the purification for it completely, complete its bowing and prostration, recite the Qurʾān in it, [perform] the tashahhud, and the prayer upon the Prophet ﷺ; this is establishing it.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَلاَ تَكُونُواْ كَالَّذِينَ قَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَهُمْ لاَ يَسْمَعُونَ﴾.
Because they listened with the listening of enmity; and His saying makes this clear: ﴿إنَّ شَرَّ الدَّوابِّ عِنْدَ اللهِ الصُمُّ البُكْمُ الَّذِينَ لاَ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
That is, they are like the deaf in that they do not hear with the hearing of one who accepts the truth, and like the dumb because they do not speak any good, nor do they understand it.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَلَوْ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِمْ خَيْراً لأَسْمَعَهُمْ﴾.
That is, He would have made them hear the answer to everything they ask about.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَلَوْ أَسْمَعَهُمْ لَتَوَلَّواْ وَّهُمْ مُّعْرِضُونَ﴾.
That is, had He informed them of everything they ask about, they would have turned away and disbelieved, out of stubbornness and envy.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱسْتَجِيبُواْ للَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda holds that the meaning of "اسْتَجِيبُوا" is "respond" (ajībū), and he recited:
وَدَاعٍ دَعَا يَا مَنْ يُجِيبُ إِلَى النَّدَى * فَلَمْ يَسْتَجِبْهُ عِنْدَ ذَاكَ مُجِيْبُ
(Many a caller has called: "O who will respond to generosity?" — and no responder answered him then.)
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿إِذَا دَعَاكُم لِمَا يُحْيِيكُمْ﴾.
That is, to that by which you attain everlasting life in the Hereafter.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَاعْلَمُواْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: He comes between the believer and disbelief, and between [the unbeliever and] faith.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He comes between the believer and disobedience, and between the unbeliever and obedience.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Some of the philologists interpreted this view as meaning: He comes between them and your sin by death.
And it has been said: It is a figure of speech, that is, He is near, as He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَنحنُ أقربُ إليه من حَبْلِ الوريد﴾.
And it has been said: They sometimes feared their enemy, so Allah, Mighty and Glorious, informed them that He comes between a man and his heart, so He replaces their fear with security, and replaces their enemy's security with fear.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَٱتَّقُواْ فِتْنَةً لاَّ تُصِيبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنكُمْ خَآصَّةً﴾.
It has been said: It encompasses the wrongdoer and others.
And Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَٱتَّقُواْ فِتْنَةً لاَّ تُصِيبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنكُمْ خَآصَّةً﴾ — he said: Allah commanded the believers not to tolerate wrongdoing in their midst, lest Allah encompass them all with punishment.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It concerns the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ specifically.
And it is narrated from al-Zubayr that he said on the day of the Camel, when he met [the enemy]: I never thought that this verse was revealed concerning us, the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ, until today: ﴿وَٱتَّقُواْ فِتْنَةً لاَّ تُصِيبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنكُمْ خَآصَّةً﴾.
And another view, which is the view of Abū l-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad], is that it is a prohibition after a command — a prohibition [addressed to] the fitna — while the meaning of the prohibition is for the wrongdoers, that is: do not come near wrongdoing. And Sībawayh reported: لا أرينَّك ها هنا ("let me not see you here"), that is, do not be here, for whoever is here I will see.
And Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] holds that its meaning is a statement (khabar), and the entry of the nūn [of emphasis] into a statement is permissible because it has the force of a conditional (jazāʾ).
Abū Jaʿfar said: And I saw ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān [al-Akhfash the Younger] holding that it is a supplication (duʿāʾ).

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَٱذْكُرُوۤاْ إِذْ أَنتُمْ قَلِيلٌ مُّسْتَضْعَفُونَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ تَخَافُونَ أَن يَتَخَطَّفَكُمُ ٱلنَّاسُ﴾.
Wahb ibn Munabbih said: By "the people" He means Persia.
And ʿIkrima said: The unbelievers of Quraysh.
Al-Suddī said: So He sheltered you in Medina.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿كَمَآ أَخْرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَيْتِكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾
There are several views on it:
(a) Al-Kisāʾī said: The meaning is: they dispute with you concerning the truth, their disputing being just as your Lord brought you out of your house with the truth.
(b) Abū ʿUbayda said: (ما) has the meaning of (الذي), that is: and [by] the One who brought you out; this is the sense of his words.
(c) And a third view: that the meaning is: Say, the anfāl belong to Allah and the Messenger, just as your Lord brought you out of your house with the truth; that is, just as your Lord brought you out of your house with the truth while they were averse, say: the anfāl belong to Allah and the Messenger, even if they are averse.
And it has been said: ﴿كَمَآ أَخْرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَيْتِكَ﴾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying, the Exalted, ﴿لَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾, that is: this promise to them is true in the Hereafter, just as your Lord brought you out of your house with the truth and fulfilled His promise to you of victory.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿يُجَادِلُونَكَ فِي ٱلْحَقِّ بَعْدَمَا تَبَيَّنَ﴾.
So just as this was true, so too everything He has promised you is true; they dispute with you concerning the truth after it has become clear. And its being made clear is that, since He informed them of one report after another from the Unseen, truly, it was incumbent that they not doubt His report.
And the best of these is the view of Mujāhid, that the meaning is: just as your Lord brought you out of your house, that is, from Medina to Badr, against [their] aversion, so they dispute with you concerning the truth; because both matters did occur, with the one being close to the other, and that is more fitting than what is far from it.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: The rain was before the drowsiness.
And one says: أَمِنَ، يأمنُ، أَمْناً، وأَمَاناً، وأَمَنَةً، وأَمْنَةً.
And it is narrated from Ibn Muḥayṣin that he read "أمْنَةً" with sukūn on the mīm.
And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: Drowsiness in prayer is from Satan, and in battle it is security (amana).
[Translator's note: the last four paragraphs concern verses 9–11 (the rain and ﴿أَمَنَةً﴾), though the source places them under this entry.]

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿يِا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إَن تَتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّكُمْ فُرْقَاناً﴾.
Mujāhid, ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, a way out.
Mujāhid said concerning His saying ﴿يَوْمَ الفُرْقَانِ﴾: He said: The day of Badr, on which Allah distinguished between truth and falsehood.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And al-furqān in the language has the meaning of al-farq (separating); one says: فرقتُ بينَ الشيئين فَرْقاً، وفُرْقاناً (I separated the two things).

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِيُثْبِتُوكَ أَوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ أَوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ﴾.
One says: أثبتُّهُ, when you have confined him.
Mujāhid said: The unbelievers wanted to do this to the Prophet ﷺ before his departure from Mecca.
And someone else said: They gathered and said: Let us confine him in a house and feed him and give him drink there; or let us all kill him together as the killing of a single man; or let us expel him so that the trouble he causes falls on others than us. And Allah, Mighty and Glorious, protected him from them.
And in the narration of Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿لِيُثْبِتُوكَ﴾ means: to bind you.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالُواْ ٱللَّهُمَّ إِن كَانَ هَـٰذَا هُوَ ٱلْحَقَّ مِنْ عِندِكَ فَأَمْطِرْ عَلَيْنَا حِجَارَةً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَوِ ٱئْتِنَا بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The one who said this was "al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Kalada".
And it is narrated that this was said in Mecca, and what indicates this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ وأَنْتَ فِيهِمْ﴾.
Several views have been given on this verse:
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that "al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith" said this — meaning: destroy us together with Muḥammad and those with him, all of us — so Allah sent down ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ وأَنْتَ فِيهمْ﴾ up to ﴿وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ﴾, that is, while among them there are people who seek forgiveness, meaning the Muslims; ﴿وَمَا لَهُمْ أَلاَّ يُعَذِّبَهُمُ اللهُ﴾ specifically [i.e. the unbelievers]; so He punished them with the sword after the Prophet ﷺ departed from them; and concerning that there was revealed ﴿سَأَلَ سَائِلٌ بِعَذَابٍ وَاقِعٍ﴾.
And al-Zuhrī narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thaʿlaba ibn Ṣuʿayr that the one who sought the decision (al-mustaftiḥ) on the day of Badr was "Abū Jahl", and that he said: "O Allah, disgrace whichever of us most severs the ties of kinship"; that was his seeking of the decision.
And ʿAṭiyya said concerning His saying, Mighty and Glorious, ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ وأَنْتَ فِيهِمْ﴾: He means the idolaters, until He brings him out from among them; ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللهُ مُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ﴾: He means the believers. He said: Then He returned to the unbelievers and said: ﴿وَمَا لَهُمْ أَلاَّ يُعَذِّبَهُم اللهُ وَهُمْ يَصُدُّونَ عَنِ المَسْجِدِ الحَرَامِ﴾?
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view, and the meaning of ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللهُ لِيُعَدِّبَهُمْ وَأَنْتَ فِيهِمْ﴾ is: Allah would not punish them while you are in their midst; and such is His way (sunna) with the nations.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ مُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ﴾. [Verse 33]
And the pronoun refers back to those of them who believed.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَمَا لَهُمْ أَلاَّ يُعَذِّبَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
That is, when you have left their midst.
And it is possible that its meaning is: and why should Allah not punish them on the Day of Resurrection?
And it has been said that its meaning is: Allah would not be punishing them were they to seek His forgiveness — without this being an affirmation that they do so; just as you say: I will never be angry with you while you obey me, that is, if you obeyed me I would not be angry with you, without it being an affirmation on your part that you obey him [Translator's note: so in the source, «لطاعته», "his obedience"].
And Mujāhid said: Its meaning is: Allah would not have punished them while they were Muslims.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the meaning of this is: Allah would not be punishing them while among them are those whose affair will end in Islam.
And it is narrated from him: and in their loins are those who will seek forgiveness.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ صَلاَتُهُمْ عِندَ ٱلْبَيْتِ إِلاَّ مُكَآءً وَتَصْدِيَةً﴾.
ʿAṭiyya narrated from Ibn ʿUmar that he said: Al-mukāʾ is whistling, and al-taṣdiya is clapping.
Ibn Shihāb said: They were mocking the believers.
And Ibn Abī Jurayj and Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated that he said: Al-mukāʾ is their putting their fingers into their mouths, and al-taṣdiya is whistling; by that they wanted to distract Muḥammad ﷺ from the prayer.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And what is known in the language is what is narrated from Ibn ʿUmar.
Abū ʿUbayd and others reported that one says: مَكَا، يَمْكُو، ومُكَاءً when he whistled, and صدَّى يُصدِّي تَصْدِيةً when he clapped.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Ibn Zayd — al-taṣdiya is their turning [people] away (ṣadd) from the religion of Allah — is far-fetched, because the verb from this is صددتُ, unless one of its two dāls is changed into yāʾ, as in تظنَّيتُ from ظَنَنْتُ; and likewise what is narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: al-taṣdiya is their turning [people] away from the House of Allah.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يُنفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ لِيَصُدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means "Abū Sufyān" and what he spent on his companions on the day of Uḥud.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَيَجْعَلَ ٱلْخَبِيثَ بَعْضَهُ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فَيَرْكُمَهُ جَمِيعاً﴾.
One says: ركمتُ الشيءَ, when you have put part of it on top of another.
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿فَيَجْعَلَهُ فِي جَهَنَّمَ﴾
That is, the wicked, so that they are punished by it.
And by "the wicked" He means the unbelievers; thus Ibn ʿAbbās said: "He distinguished the people of felicity from the people of wretchedness, that is, by settling these in the Garden and those in the Fire."
That is, He puts the unbelievers one on top of another and makes them a heap, that is, He gathers them one to another until they are many. ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ﴾: He referred it back to the unbelievers, and He referred ﴿فَيَجْعَلَهُ﴾ back to "the wicked" according to its wording, so that they are punished by it, as the Exalted said: ﴿فَتُكْوَى بِهَا جِبَاهُهُمْ وَجُنُوبُهُمْ وَظُهُورُهُمْ﴾.
* And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِنْ يَعُودُواْ فَقَدْ مَضَتْ سُنَّةُ الأَوَّلِينَ﴾. [Verse 38]
Mujāhid said: The day of Badr, [and what happened] to the nations before that; for Allah, Mighty and Glorious, has distinguished between truth and falsehood.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَقَاتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّىٰ لاَ تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾.
The meaning is: until there is no fitna of disbelief; and what indicates this ellipsis is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَيَكُونَ الدِّينُ كُلُّهُ لله﴾

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ فَٱعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَوْلاَكُمْ نِعْمَ ٱلْمَوْلَىٰ وَنِعْمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ﴾.
That is, and if they return to disbelief and to enmity towards you, ﴿فَٱعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَوْلاَكُمْ﴾, that is, your protector and your helper, so their enmity will not harm you.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَٱعْلَمُوۤا أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُمْ مِّن شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ للَّهِ خُمُسَهُ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْيَتَامَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَاكِينِ وَٱبْنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾.
There is disagreement about the meaning of this verse:
Some said: The fifth [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense requires "the booty"] is divided into five parts: four of them are for the duration of the month of war [Translator's note: so in the source, «لمدة شهر الحرب»; probably a corruption of «لمن شهد الحرب», "for those who were present at the battle"], and one of them is divided into five; whatever of it was for the Messenger is put where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to put it.
And it is narrated that he used to put it towards strengthening the Muslims; and four [parts] are for the near kin, the orphans, the needy and the wayfarer. This is the position of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him.
And some of them said: This share, despite its smallness, is divided into parts for the poor, the needy and the wayfarer, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity." This is the position of Abū Ḥanīfa.
And some of them said: If the imām sees fit to give these mentioned [categories], he gives them; and if he sees that others are more deserving than they, he gives those. He said: If their being mentioned as having shares required that it not go outside their totality, it would not be permissible, when a group is mentioned, to give some of them and not others; yet Allah, Mighty and Glorious, has said: ﴿إنَّما الصَّدّقَاتُ للفُقَرَاءِ، والمساكين﴾ to the end of the verse, and were it given to some of them and not others it would be permissible; rather they were mentioned because they are among the most important of those to be given.
And He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿قُلْ مَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ خَيْر فَلِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالأَقْرَبِينَ﴾.
And he may give to others than those named. This is the position of Mālik.
As for the meaning of ﴿فَأَنَّ للَّهِ﴾, it is an opening of speech. "Qays ibn Muslim al-Jadabī" said: I asked al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad about ﴿وَٱعْلَمُوۤا أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُمْ مِّن شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ للَّهِ خُمُسَهُ﴾, and he said: It is an opening of speech; Allah has no share; to Allah belong this world and the Hereafter.
"Abū Jaʿfar related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Samāʿa related to us, saying: Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Abū Jaʿfar related to us, from al-Rabīʿ, from Abū l-ʿĀliya: ﴿وَٱعْلَمُوۤا أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُمْ مِّن شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ للَّهِ خُمُسَهُ﴾.
He said: The booty would be brought and set down, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would divide it into five shares. He would set one share aside and divide the four among the people. Then he would put his hand into the whole share he had set aside, and whatever he grasped of it he assigned to the Kaʿba; that is what is named "for Allah". And he would say: Do not assign a share to Allah, for to Allah belong this world and the Hereafter." He said: Then the share he had set aside is divided into five shares: a share for the Prophet ﷺ, a share for the near kin, a share for the orphans, a share for the needy, and a share for the wayfarer.
And it has been said: The meaning of ﴿فَأَنَّ للَّهِ خُمُسَهُ﴾ is: then [its fifth] is for the way of Allah, like ﴿واسألِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ [Translator's note: i.e. with the muḍāf omitted].
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِن كُنتُمْ آمَنْتُمْ بِٱللَّهِ﴾
That is, if you have believed in Allah, then accept what He has commanded you.
And it has been said: The meaning is: know that Allah is your protector and your helper, if you have believed in Him.
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَمَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَىٰ عَبْدِنَا يَوْمَ ٱلْفُرْقَانِ يَوْمَ ٱلْتَقَى ٱلْجَمْعَانِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is the day of Badr, on which Allah distinguished between truth and falsehood.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِذْ أَنتُمْ بِالْعُدْوَةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُم بِٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلْقُصْوَىٰ﴾.
Qatāda said: Al-ʿudwa is the edge of the valley, and so it is in the language.
And the meaning of "الدُّنْيَا" is: the one adjoining Medina; and the meaning of "القُصْوَى" is: the one adjoining Mecca. Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱلرَّكْبُ أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: He means the caravan that was with Abū Sufyān.
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿لِّيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَن بَيِّنَةٍ وَيَحْيَىٰ مَنْ حَيَّ عَن بَيِّنَةٍ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Ibn Abī Isḥāq said: He made the rightly guided like the living, and made the one astray like the perishing. He said: That is, so that whoever disbelieves disbelieves after the proof, through what he saw of the sign and the lesson, and whoever believes believes on the like of that.
And someone else said: "So that he may perish" means: so that whoever dies may die with a proof of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, against him that has cut off his excuse, and whoever of them lives may live on the like of that. ﴿وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَسَمِيعٌ﴾ to your words when you left them, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of what your souls conceal.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِذْ يُرِيكَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي مَنَامِكَ قَلِيلاً وَلَوْ أَرَاكَهُمْ كَثِيراً لَّفَشِلْتُمْ وَلَتَنَازَعْتُمْ فِي ٱلأَمْرِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said, from Mujāhid: The Prophet ﷺ saw them in sleep as few, and he related the dream to his Companions, and Allah made them firm by that.
And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said:
The meaning is: when Allah showed them to you with your eye with which you sleep.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the meaning on this view is: in the place of your sleep.
And the first view is better, for two reasons:
One of them: what is narrated, that the Prophet ﷺ saw them in sleep.
And the other: in His saying ﴿وَإِذْ يُرِيكُمُوهُمْ إِذِ التَقَيْتُمْ فِي أَعْيُنِكُمْ﴾; so the first seeing was in sleep, and the second at the encounter.
And what al-Ḥasan said is possible, though far-fetched, on the basis that His saying ﴿إِذْ يريكُمُوهُمْ﴾ is an address to the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions.
And the meaning [of "and He made you few in their eyes"] is: so that they would not make preparations against you, because of what Allah, Mighty and Glorious, intended of the Muslims' victory over them.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَلاَ تَنَازَعُواْ فَتَفْشَلُواْ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: One says: فَشِلَ يَفْشَل فَشَلاً, when he is afraid to advance, out of cowardice.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, your victory.
And Maʿmar said, from Qatāda: That is, the wind of war.
And what is known in the language is that one says: ذهبتْ ريحُهم, that is, their power (dawla).

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَلاَ تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ خَرَجُواْ مِن دِيَارِهِم بَطَراً وَرِئَآءَ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾.
He means Abū Jahl and his companions on the day of Badr.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِذْ زَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾ [Verse 48].
He said: The meaning is: and remember when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He came to them on the day of Badr with his banner and his troops, and cast into their hearts that they would not be defeated, while they were fighting for the religion of their fathers.
* And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿فَلَمَّا تَرَآءَتِ ٱلْفِئَتَانِ﴾.
That is, they met, until each of them saw the other.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿نَكَصَ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ﴾
That is, he went back retreating; and one says: نَكَصَ على عقبيه, when he went back the way he came.
﴿وَقَالَ إِنِّي بَرِيۤءٌ مِّنْكُمْ إِنَّيۤ أَرَىٰ مَا لاَ تَرَوْنَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He saw the angels. ﴿إِنَّيۤ أَخَافُ ٱللَّهَ وَٱللَّهُ شَدِيدُ ٱلْعِقَابِ﴾.
It has been said: He only feared that the time to which he had been granted respite had arrived.
And it has been said: Rather, he lied.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, like the doing [of]. And al-daʾb according to the philologists is: habit; and its real sense according to them is that it comes from your saying فلانٌ يَدأبُ, that is, he persists in a thing and keeps to it; and this is the meaning of habit.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ عَاهَدْتَّ مِنْهُمْ ثُمَّ يَنقُضُونَ عَهْدَهُمْ فِي كُلِّ مَرَّةٍ وَهُمْ لاَ يَتَّقُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the Banū Qurayẓa.

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿فَإِمَّا تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ فِي ٱلْحَرْبِ﴾.
That is, [if] you come upon them and overcome them; ﴿فَشَرِّدْ بِهِم مَّنْ خَلْفَهُمْ﴾
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: That is, warn by means of them those who are behind them. And Abū ʿUbayd said: It is the dialect of Quraysh: "شرِّدْ بهم" means: make an example of them for others to hear of.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, make a deterrent example of them.
And al-tashrīd in the language is: scattering and dispersing.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِمَّا تَخَافَنَّ مِن قَوْمٍ خِيَانَةً﴾.
That is, deceit and breaking of the covenant. ﴿فَٱنْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلَىٰ سَوَآءٍ﴾, that is, throw back to them [the knowledge of] their breaking of their covenant, so that you and they are on an equal footing in knowledge. One says: نبذتُ إليه على سواءٍ, that is, I informed him that I had come to know from him what he had concealed.
And ʿUmar ibn ʿAnbasa [Translator's note: the source has «عمر بن عَنْبَة»; the Companion who narrates this ḥadīth is usually given as ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasa] narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever has a covenant with a people for a term, let him neither tighten a knot nor undo it until its term expires, or he throws it back to them on an equal footing."

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَبَقُوۤاْ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: That is, they escaped. * Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ لاَ يُعْجِزُونَ﴾. It is narrated from Ibn Muḥayṣin that he read (لا يُعَجِّزُونِ) with doubling and with kasra on the nūn.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is an error in two respects:
One of them: that the meaning of عجَّزه is: he deemed him weak and deemed his affair weak.
And the other: that it would have had to be with two nūns.
And the meaning of أَعْجَزَه is: he outstripped him and escaped him so that he had no power over him.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَأَعِدُّواْ لَهُمْ مَّا ٱسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِّن قُوَّةٍ وَمِن رِّبَاطِ ٱلْخَيْلِ تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِ عَدْوَّ ٱللَّهِ وَعَدُوَّكُمْ﴾.
ʿIkrima said: "Strength" is the stallions, and "tethered horses" are the mares.
And someone else said: "Strength" is weaponry. And ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "﴿وَأَعِدُّواْ لَهُمْ مَّا ٱسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِّن قُوَّةٍ﴾ — indeed, strength is shooting."
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَآخَرِينَ مِن دُونِهِمْ لاَ تَعْلَمُونَهُمُ﴾.
That is, and you strike terror into others, that is, you make them afraid.
Mujāhid said: They are the Banū Qurayẓa. And Ibn Zayd said: They are the hypocrites. And it has been said: They are the jinn. And al-Suddī said: The people of Persia.

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِن جَنَحُواْ لِلسَّلْمِ فَٱجْنَحْ لَهَا﴾.
جَنَحُوا: they inclined. And Abū ʿAmr said: al-salam is peace-making, and al-silm is Islam.
And Abū ʿUbayda holds that al-silm, al-salm and al-salam [all mean]: peace-making.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِن يُرِيدُوۤاْ أَن يَخْدَعُوكَ﴾.
That is, by outwardly showing [a desire for] peace. ﴿فَإِنَّ حَسْبَكَ ٱللَّهُ﴾, that is, He is sufficient for you; هُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَيَّدَكَ بِنَصْرِهِ وَبِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ}, that is, He strengthened you and united their hearts.
And this is one of the great signs, because one of them would be slapped with a single slap and [his people] would fight on his behalf until they exacted retaliation for it; and they were the fiercest of Allah's creatures in tribal zeal. Then when the Prophet ﷺ was sent, one of them would fight his own brother over Islam.
Abū Jaʿfar related to us, saying: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad related to us in al-Anbār, saying: Naṣr ibn ʿAlī related to us, saying: My father related to me, saying: Shuʿba related to us, saying: Bashīr ibn Thābit, of the family of al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, informed us concerning His saying ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَيَّدَكَ بِنَصرِهِ وَبِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ until he reached ﴿إِنَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾: He said: It was revealed concerning the Anṣār.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ حَسْبُكَ ٱللَّهُ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
That is, Allah suffices you and suffices those who follow you.
And it has been said: The meaning is: and those who follow you help you.

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ حَرِّضِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَى ٱلْقِتَالِ﴾.
Al-taḥrīḍ is intense urging, and it is taken from al-ḥaraḍ, which is being close to perishing; that is, urge them until whoever opposes knows that he has come close to perishing.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿إِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صَابِرُونَ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: It was made obligatory on a man to fight ten; then it was made easier for them, and He said: ﴿الآنَ خَفَّفَ اللهُ عَنْكُمْ﴾ up to His saying ﴿واللهُ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾, and it was prescribed for them that a hundred should not flee from two hundred.
Ibn Shubruma said: And I consider enjoining the right and forbidding the wrong to be likewise.
And al-Aʿmash narrated, from Marw ibn Murra [Translator's note: so in the source; the narrator is ʿAmr ibn Murra], from Abū ʿUbayda, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: "When it was the day of Badr, the captives were brought, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: What do you think about these captives? Abū Bakr said: O Messenger of Allah, they are your people and your stock; spare them, perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness. And ʿUmar said: O Messenger of Allah, they called you a liar, drove you out and fought you; bring them forward and strike their necks." And he mentioned the ḥadīth, and in it he said: So Allah sent down:
﴿مَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَن يَكُونَ لَهُ أَسْرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ يُثْخِنَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
﴿مَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَن يَكُونَ لَهُ أَسْرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ يُثْخِنَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Al-ithkhān is: killing.
And it has been said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يُثْخِنَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: until he goes to great lengths in killing his enemies.
And it has been said: until he is firmly established in the land.
And al-ithkhān in the language is: strength and severity.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿لَّوْلاَ كِتَابٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ سَبَقَ لَمَسَّكُمْ فِيمَآ أَخَذْتُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾.
There are several views on it:
Mujāhid said: It had gone before from Allah that He would make the spoils lawful for them.
And Abū Jaʿfar said: What strengthens this is that Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated from Abū Hurayra from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Spoils were not made lawful for any black-headed people before us; a fire used to descend from the sky and consume them. Then when it was the day of Badr, the people fell into what they fell into, so Allah, Mighty and Glorious, sent down ﴿لَّوْلاَ كِتَابٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ سَبَقَ﴾ up to His saying ﴿إنَّ اللهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾."
And it has been said: It had gone before from Allah, Mighty and Glorious, that He would forgive the people of Badr their past and future sins. Al-Ḥasan said that; Ashʿath narrated it from him.
And Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn narrated from him that he said: It had gone before from Allah, Mighty and Glorious, that He would not punish a people except after a prior warning, and He had not warned them beforehand concerning it.
And Sālim narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: ﴿لَّوْلاَ كِتَابٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ سَبَقَ﴾ — he said: for the people of Badr, of felicity — ﴿لَمَسَّكُمْ فِيمَآ أَخَذْتُمْ﴾ a great punishment from Allah.
And it has been said: It had gone before from Allah that He forgives minor sins to whoever avoids major sins.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لِّمَن فِيۤ أَيْدِيكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلأَسْرَىٰ إِن يَعْلَمِ ٱللَّهُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ خَيْراً يُؤْتِكُمْ خَيْراً مِّمَّآ أُخِذَ مِنكُمْ﴾.
It has been said: in the Hereafter. And it has been said: He will compensate you in this world.
And it is narrated from al-ʿAbbās that he said: "I was taken captive on the day of Badr with twenty ounces (ūqiyya) on me, and they were taken from me; then Allah compensated me with twenty slaves and promised me forgiveness."

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِن يُرِيدُواْ خِيَانَتَكَ فَقَدْ خَانُواْ ٱللَّهَ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
"خيانتك" (betraying you), that is, breaking the covenant.

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَهَاجَرُواْ وَجَاهَدُواْ بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
It has been said that one says: هاجر الرجل, when the man went out from one land to another.
And it has been said: One only says هَجَرَ and هَاجَرَ فلانٌ because when a man embraced Islam his people would shun him and he would shun them; then, if he feared trial for himself, he would depart from them, and his journey was called hijra.
And it has been said: هاجر, because he was in a state of shunning his people and their shunning him, so he is a muhājir; he left the abode of his people and his homeland and departed to the abode of Islam. And they are two hijras: the first emigrants are those who emigrated to the land of Abyssinia, and the others those who emigrated to Medina up to the time of the Conquest.
And the hijra came to an end, because the abode is all of it the abode of Islam, so there is no hijra. This is the view of the ḥadīth scholars and of those whose knowledge is trusted.
* And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَلَمْ يُهَاجِرُواْ مَا لَكُمْ مِّن وَلاَيَتِهِم مِّن شَيْءٍ﴾.
That is, of helping them and inheriting from them.
Qatāda said: A man would take another man as a brother and say: You inherit from me and I inherit from you. Then that was abrogated by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَأُولُوا الأرْحَامِ بَعْضُهمْ أَوْلَى ببَعْض في كِتَابِ اللهِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَٱلَّذينَ كَفَرُواْ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ إِلاَّ تَفْعَلُوهُ﴾.
And the meaning of "إِنْ لاَ تَفْعَلُوهُ" is: if you do not do [the] helping and the mutual alliance.
And Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿إِلاَّ تَفْعَلُوهُ﴾ — he said: He is saying: unless you act in inheritance according to what I have commanded you.
And Ibn Zayd said: That is, unless you leave them to inherit from one another as they used to.
Mujāhid said: This is abrogated; it was abrogated by ﴿وَأُولُوا الأرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَى بِبَعضٍ﴾.
And it is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr that he said: This concerns the agnatic heirs (al-ʿaṣabāt); a man would make a pact with another man that they would inherit from each other, and that was abrogated. And it has been said: The [Qurʾānic] shares of inheritance (al-farāʾiḍ) abrogated it.
And most of the narrators hold that what abrogated it is ﴿وأُولوا الأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ﴾, the verse.
And Sufyān narrated from al-Suddī from Abū Mālik, who said: A man said: Shall we let our idolater kinsmen inherit? So there was revealed ﴿وَٱلَّذينَ كَفَرُواْ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ﴾. And Yūnus narrated from al-Ḥasan, who said: "The Bedouin would not inherit from an emigrant until there was revealed ﴿وأُولُوا الأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَى بِبَعْضٍ في كِتَابِ الله﴾. So it has become clear that the meaning of the verse is that blood relatives inherit from one another by their kinship, to the exclusion of those who had made alliances with them, and that this abrogated the inheriting by alliance that preceded it."
